article_title: ChainDrop Worm Compromises Over 1,300 npm Package Versions After keyv Maintainer's GitHub Account Is Breached

content_preview.title: ChainDrop Worm Compromises Over 1,300 npm Package Versions After keyv Maintainer's GitHub Account Is Breached
content_preview.summary: A self-propagating worm hijacked keyv and related npm packages on August 4 after a maintainer's GitHub account was breached, spreading to 1,300+ package versions.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

A self-propagating worm compromised dozens of widely used npm packages beginning August 4, 2026, after attackers took over the GitHub account of jaredwray, the maintainer behind the caching library keyv, according to [Snyk](https://snyk.io/blog/inside-keyv-npm-compromise-preinstall-malware-trusted-provenance-ide-hooks/) and [DevOps.com](https://devops.com/fast-moving-shai-hulud-attack-infects-npm-packages-with-2-billion-monthly-downloads/). [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.co...

editor_notes.content_quality: Thorough, well-organized News piece (1,113 words) with clear sub-headed sections (initial breach, payload mechanics, self-propagation/exfiltration, scale/lineage, recommendations) appropriate for a fast-moving, multi-source security incident. Represents the most current and comprehensive state of the story (through the August 6 CSA advisory update).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 6 sources in full, including the two also covering this story in the companion submission (PR #2141), plus two unique to this submission (DevOps.com, CSA Singapore advisory). SecurityWeek: confirms the 2,200+ versions/440 packages initial count, the 'evolved descendant of the Shai-Hulud 2.0 worm' / EtherHiding quote verbatim. Wiz: confirms the 'descendant of the \'Mini\' Shai-Hulud malware family' quote verbatim, the Claude/OpenAI/Codex/Cursor/Gemini credential targets, Jenkins master.key, Kubernetes/Vault/cryptocurrency-wallet/etc-shadow targets, and the 'Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again' exfil-repo description. Snyk: confirms the 09:35:00 UTC keyv@6.0.0 publish time, the exact package list with versions, the 29,918-byte setup.mjs and 727,680-byte Math_Symbol.js figures (rounding to the article's 'roughly 30-kilobyte' and '728 kilobytes'), and the provenance-boundary quote verbatim. Aikido: confirms the eleven-package list with exact version numbers, the 200-glob-pattern credential scan, the 50-branches/'chore: update config' GitHub App token abuse, the ~1,300 exfil-repo count, the npm-cache[.]com domain, the August 5 'At least 444 packages (across 1381 versions)' update, and the @deliveroo/@picsart/@qlik downstream package names (found in a 'spread to other maintainers' list — confirmed present despite an initial case-sensitive search miss). DevOps.com: confirms the Makari and Kiran Raj quotes verbatim, the 728 KB Math_Symbol.js figure, and the Deliveroo/OneReach/ServiceTitan/Picsart/Qlik organization list with the '50 to 100 newly infected packages every few minutes' figure. CSA Singapore advisory: confirms the 1,300+ versions/2 billion downloads August 6 figures and all four verbatim remediation-action quotes. The internal link to the May 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud article resolves to an existing published article. No misattributions or hallucinated quotes found across any of the 6 sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked (timestamps, byte sizes, package/version lists, org names, quotes, advisory recommendations) traces exactly to its cited source, including several highly specific technical details (exact byte counts, npm-cache[.]com registration date, branch-commit-author details) that could easily have been garbled but were not.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and precise throughout; appropriately hedges in 'What We Don't Know' on the unresolved initial-access vector and the fact that every source's count was a moving target during an active campaign.
editor_notes.originality: Substantially overlaps with the companion submission PR #2141 ('ChainDrop Worm Hijacks keyv and cacheable npm Packages, Spreading to 440 Packages in Under Four Hours') — both cover the same ChainDrop/keyv npm supply-chain compromise. This submission is materially more complete and current: it incorporates the August 5 Aikido update and the August 6 CSA Singapore advisory (neither of which PR #2141 cites), names specific downstream-affected organizations, gives exact timestamps and byte-level payload details, and — critically — its quotes were all verified verbatim with correct attribution, whereas PR #2141 was found to contain a pattern of quote-fidelity problems (see PR #2141's review). Approving this submission as the definitive, most current, and most accurate account of the incident; rejecting PR #2141 as both a duplicate and independently quote-fidelity-deficient.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, thoroughly-sourced, and current submission — the most complete account of the ChainDrop npm supply-chain incident among the two competing submissions received. Approving outright.
